newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish 1997 gross funding requirement 2.6 bln punts.
newsitem.headline: Irish 1997 gross funding requirement 2.6 bln punts.

text.p: Ireland's National Treasury Mangement Agency (NTMA) announced an indicative gross funding requirement to be met from Irish pound bonds and Exchequer notes of not more than 2.6 billion punts in 1997.

This is the first time the agency, which manages Ireland's national debt, has released an estimate of the gross funding requirement. It will be reviewed at the end of each quarter and the NTMA will inform the market of any change.
"It's part of a move toward greater transparency," an NTMA spokesman told Reuters.
The NTMA has already told the market that it can expect 10 bond auctions between February and November this year.

The auctions will be held on the third Tuesday of each month and a minimum 100 million Irish pounds will be auctioned each time. The NTMA has also said it will give five working day's notice of each auction.
The first auction is due to be held on Tuesday, February 18 and the NTMA will announce the amount and maturity of stock to be auctioned next Tuesday, February 11.
